scope: Proposition 3.5 (Fixed-separation initialization) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In this setting, let n ≥ 3 and fix B > 0, d > 0 and η > 0. For all sufficiently small λ, the data (3.11) have a product-solution continuation to a neighborhood of {(x, y) : |x|, |y| ≤ B, |x − y| ≥ d}. Every fixed Cm norm on a smaller neighborhood is bounded uniformly in λ. The continuation agrees with G1,λ where yn < −η and with G2,λ where xn < −η, on the corresponding overlaps. The smallness threshold for λ and the constants may depend on B, d, η, m.
